A1.justification: Despite the changed title and publication format, both PDFs describe the same MIS benchmarking and serialization study. All 28 pages of v2 and 33 pages of v3, including appendices, support comparison through readable text and inspectable figures.

before.justification: v2 reports original solver benchmarks, serialization measurements, and local-search experiments on synthetic and real-world graphs.

after.justification: v3 retains the original empirical benchmarks and analyses, including their appendix results, and reports additional BA serialization percentages in Figure 2.

M1.justification: The degree-based serialization procedure in Algorithm 1, LwD pseudo-natural serialization, and local-search procedure remain unchanged. The new code documentation does not establish a new algorithm, architecture, or learning objective.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate MIS on ER and BA graphs, RB-small/RB-large, REDDIT-MULTI-5K, and COLLAB, including the same large-graph coverage. Additional graph generators listed in v3 Appendix D are software capabilities, not evidence of additional evaluated datasets.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain Deg-Greedy, OnlineMIS, ReduMIS, iSCO, PCQO, LwD, LTFT, DIFUSCO, and DiffUCO, with Ran-Greedy retained in the large-graph and ratio analyses. New citations and relocated comparison displays do not add evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: The training/test graph counts, distribution matching, best-of-20 solution sampling, training settings, and resource allocations remain as documented in Appendix B. v3 Table 1 consolidates existing resource information. The serialization repetition-count revision is assessed under E5; the underlying evaluation design is retained.

E4.justification: v3 Figure 2 adds a BA serialization summary with different agreement estimates for the existing analysis of alignment with greedy choices. This is a limited revision to the reported analysis. The LTFT comparison, LwD pseudo-natural serialization, local-search experiments, and full appendix analysis plots are retained.

E5.justification: v2 Section 5.2 reports 1,000 serialization repetitions, whereas v3 Section 4.2 reports 100. v2 Appendix C.5 already stated 100, so this resolves a reporting inconsistency without establishing an actual change in runs performed. No confidence intervals, significance tests, or training-seed uncertainty reporting are added.

E6.justification: The matched benchmark and local-search tables have unchanged numerical entries. However, for BA graphs with n=1000 and m=15, Deg-Greedy's three serialization percentages are 90/93/79 in v2 Figure 4 and 86/85/76 in the new v3 Figure 2 panel. v3 Figure 5 retains the earlier values. These are newly reported, inconsistent estimates, not an established same-setting performance change.

T1.justification: v3 Section 4.4 adds explicit conditions d>exp(20) and n>exp(40), attributed to the cited theorem's proof, to distinguish practical graph sizes from the asymptotic regime. The MIS definition, PCQO objective, asymptotic expressions, and serialization mathematics otherwise remain unchanged; no new proof is supplied.

C1.justification: The central claims about classical solver performance and serialization are retained. v2 Appendix D cautiously says the empirical ratios bring an asymptotic conjecture into doubt; v3 makes the stronger practical-size inapplicability claim an explicit contribution in the abstract and introduction.

C2.justification: v3 reclassifies PCQO as showing consistently low greedy agreement, whereas v2 grouped its rising agreement pattern with better-performing methods. It also suggests that LwD's multiple-node decisions may approximate local search and expands the finite-size explanation. Conversely, v2 Section 7's substantive qualifications about fast inference, strict deadlines, and application-dependent algorithm choice are removed.

D1.justification: New Appendix D reports a public implementation and documents generation scripts, graph and solution formats, greedy implementations, analysis entry points, local-search integration, and external solver repositories. v2 already supplied extensive experimental settings but lacked this documented code release and reproduction workflow.

R1.justification: v3 adds works including Garmendia et al. on neural improvement heuristics, d O Costa et al. on learned 2-opt, and Alkhouri et al. (2022), while removing references including Balcan et al., Nair et al., and Hespe et al. It also explicitly discusses the narrow empirical scope of Angelini and Ricci-Tersenghi. The updated PCQO publication reference represents the same evaluated method.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, and concluding narrative are extensively rewritten. Related work moves after the experiments, graph descriptions receive dedicated main-text subsections, and the issue–solution and alternative-views structure is replaced by a conclusion and takeaways. The appendices are reorganized around the retained analyses and new code documentation.

P2.justification: v3 adds the resource-summary table, moves BA/RB/real-world benchmark tables into the main text, combines the ER and BA LTFT heatmaps, adds a BA serialization panel, and redisplays selected ratio heatmaps in the main text. Typography, headers, page geometry, and figure placement change throughout, while many underlying displays and table entries are retained.

improvement.justification: The new code/data documentation and resource summary improve reproducibility and accessibility. However, the added BA panel disagrees with the retained appendix, and the revised description of PCQO as consistently low-agreement conflicts with its unchanged rising profile in Figure 2. Removing the speed-versus-quality qualifications also reduces balance. These documentation gains and scientific-exposition weaknesses leave the net quality direction unclear.
